meta.purpose: Fear/sadness/happiness change curves grounded in human affective science — not free drift to 0/1.

papers.cite: Rescorla & Wagner (1972) — prediction-error learning; negatively accelerated acquisition/extinction.
papers.use: Fear falls fast at first then slows; extinction often incomplete (context/residual V).

papers.cite: Bouton — extinction = new inhibitory learning, not erasure; renewal/spontaneous recovery.
papers.use: Safety never deletes original abandonment engram; asymptote stays above zero.

papers.cite: Dugan, Fraley et al. — attachment anxiety declines early then plateaus (canalization).
papers.use: Partner-specific anxiety drops modestly then stabilizes; not a decade-long crash.

papers.cite: Chopik et al. — attachment anxiety declines slowly across adulthood; being in a relationship helps but residual remains.
papers.use: Longitudinal mean change is gradual, not 0.9→0.3 in a few good years.

papers.cite: Davidson — affective chronometry: rise/peak/recovery limbs of emotion.
papers.use: Negative recovery can be slow (stickiness); well-being ≠ never feeling fear.

papers.cite: Verduyn / Scherer — emotion duration rank: fear often shorter episode than sadness; joy mid.
papers.use: Momentary fear spikes vs lasting sadness/mood set differently from trait fear.

papers.cite: Lykken & Tellegen / Brickman hedonic treadmill; revised set-point theory.
papers.use: Cheer/happiness regresses toward set-point; lasting uplift is partial.

papers.cite: Baumeister / Rozin — bad stronger than good; threat learning outpaces safety learning.

not_abandoned.note: soft residual; healthy decade can reach ~0.35
